audits.claim: The catchphrase 四十八茶百鼠 is figurative ('many', not a count) and is a later label of the traditional-colour literature rather than a located Edo-period document (NDL レファレンス協同データベース no. 1000168280; 長崎盛輝 1988; 吉岡幸雄 2000).
audits.source_locator: レファレンス事例詳細 「四十八茶百鼠（しじゅうはっちゃひゃくねず）」とは何か… (提供館 福岡市総合図書館; 登録番号 1000168280; 登録 2015-02-26; 解決), 回答 section, first cited item 『色の用語事典』 p.218; same record's 参考資料 list carries 吉岡幸雄『日本の色辞典』(紫紅社, 2000, ISBN 4879405493, p.238 cited in 回答) and 長崎盛輝『日本の伝統色彩』(京都書院, 1988, ISBN 4763630776, p.200-203 〈附説〉 cited in 回答)
audits.source_excerpt: 江戸時代にさまざまな茶色や灰色が大流行したことを表わす言葉であり、四十八や百は実際の数ではなく多いことを意味している。
audits.retrieval_method: Session fetch tool only. The NDL Collaborative Reference Database record was retrieved as a Wayback Machine copy (the live site returns HTTP 403 on both prior URL forms; not scraped); the retrieved page matches the cited registration number 1000168280. Corroborating lexical retrievals from kotobank.jp word pages: 鼠色 (デジタル大辞泉; 精選版日本国語大辞典; 講談社色名がわかる辞典) — kotobank has no standalone 四十八茶百鼠 entry page (HTTP 404), its site search needs JavaScript; Bing/Mojeek/DuckDuckGo bot-blocked; WebSearch quota-blocked; NDL catalogue metadata not needed beyond the record's own 参考資料 lines.
audits.basis: PASSAGE RETRIEVED verbatim from the named institutional record, so the entry's citation is accurate and checkable. (1) Figurative half: the record's answer states verbatim that 四十八や百は実際の数ではなく多いことを意味している — 'many', not a count — matching the entry exactly. (2) Citations: both parenthetical items are in the record — 吉岡幸雄 2000 (日本の色辞典, p.238: people reacted to the shogunate's 奢侈禁止令 by varying subdued 茶/黒/鼠 shades and naming them after kabuki actors and landscapes) and 長崎盛輝 1988 (日本の伝統色彩, pp.200-203, where the 〈附説〉 gives the 「四十八茶、百鼠」 呼び名) — same years and ISBNs as the record lists. (3) 'Later label rather than a located Edo document': the record's entire answer is built on five modern publications (1988-2006: 長谷井 2006, 吉岡 2000, 城 1993, 木村 1997, 長崎盛輝 1988) and frames the phrase as a label ABOUT the Edo vogue (「…大流行したことを表わす言葉」, 「四十八茶に百鼠」といわれる, 「四十八茶、百鼠」の呼び名) while citing no Edo-period primary document for the phrase itself. (4) Independent lexical corroboration, same session: 講談社色名がわかる辞典 (kotobank 鼠色) reads the phrase figuratively (「四十八茶百鼠」といわれるように多くの派生した色を生み出した) and ties it to the sumptuary context with its own hedge (茶/鼠/紺系統は許された「とされる」), matching the entry's 'is credited with' framing; 精選版日本国語大辞典 dates 鼠色 lexically to 室町末-近世初 (first attestation in 虎明本狂言), i.e. the colour word predates the Edo vogue label. Distinctions kept: modern label (the catchphrase, located in 1988-2006 literature) vs historical attire (Edo dress culture the label describes, via 吉岡's 奢侈禁止令 answer text) vs lexical category (茶-/鼠- as productive colour-name families — 藍鼠・梅鼠・銀鼠・茶鼠・利休鼠 — with 鼠色 itself a noun, glossed 灰色 in 大辞泉).
audits.coupling_implication: Era/dress coupling (entry line 53) is now inspectable from retrieved text: Edo sumptuary austerity → diversified muted 茶/鼠 shade naming is documented by the record's 吉岡幸雄 citation and by 色名がわかる辞典, with the dictionaries' own hedges preserved (許された「とされる」); the number reading is definitively figurative, so no worldbuilding system should treat 四十八/百 as inventory counts. Language/lexicon coupling: the phrase is a modern meta-label over an Edo-period naming culture, not itself an attested Edo-era lexical item in anything retrieved.
audits.limits: The record does not explicitly assert the phrase's absence from Edo-period documents; 'later label' rests on the record's modern-literature-only sourcing and framing, so the negative half of the entry's wording remains an entry-side inference consistent with everything retrieved, not a checked attestation gap.
